flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the Ponziani. You gave me a blank verdict and zero reasons. The whole point of c3 is to support d4 and build a pawn center — not a mystery 'strongest move' after a 35-centipawn swing. I cannot learn an opening from a shrug.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to c5 is a mistake, but moving your pawn to d5 would be better because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: Lichess calls this an inaccuracy; you called it a mistake, then sold ...d5 as generic center-control. Against c3 the point of ...d5 is to blow open the center before White's knight can use c3. Same because-clause as e4/e5. I already know pawns like the middle.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: d4 is why we played c3. It occupies the center and hits the c5-bishop (and e5). My king is still on e1; opening the middle does not 'keep the king safer.' You picked the king_safer bank line and skipped the only idea in the position.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: I recaptured. Material is equal. Calling this 'undefended' / wins_material is a lie — Black just took on d4 and I took back. Teach the pawn center (d4+e4), not a free pawn that was never free.

flags.quote: Moving your c5-bishop to b6 is the strongest move because it saves your b6-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop is on c5. d4 is attacking it. I am running away to b6. You named the destination square as if a b6-bishop already existed and needed saving. This is the saves_piece + move.to bug and it reads like a joke.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to e2 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Black just pinned my knight to the queen with ...Bg4. Be2 breaks the pin. You had development in the reasons and printed nothing. If you cannot say 'unpin,' do not call this the strongest move with a blank because.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b4 is playable, but moving your pawn to h3 would be better.
flags.critique: Better how? h3 asks the pinned bishop a question. b4 kicks the other bishop and weakens the queenside. Empty reasons, empty because. 'There's better' plus a SAN is not a lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Two plies ago you wanted h3 and refused to say why. Now I play it and you still refuse. I am putting the question to the g4-bishop that pins Nf3. Name the pin.

flags.quote: Moving your g4-bishop to h5 is the strongest move because it saves your h5-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: Same destination-square gag as Bb6. The bishop is on g4, h3 attacks it, I keep the pin by sliding to h5. There is no h5-bishop until I get there. Say I am keeping the pin, not saving a piece that lives on the square I just moved to.

flags.quote: Moving your a1-rook to c1 is playable, but moving your pawn to g4 would be better.
flags.critique: You mentioned a semi-open file for the move I played and gave g4 zero chess. g4 hits the h5-bishop again and gains kingside space. If the alternative is the lesson, explain the alternative.

flags.quote: Moving your h5-bishop to g6 is a mistake, but moving your f8-rook to e8 would be better because it gives your rook a semi-open file.
flags.critique: 118 centipawns and you will not tell me why ...Bg6 is wrong. Re8 'gets a semi-open file' is phrase-bank filler — every rook move onto an e-file would get that line. What did I hang, what break did I allow, what was the threat?

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 leaves your pawn hanging to the black f6-knight and g6-bishop. A better move would have been moving your e2-bishop to d3 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: I just pushed d5. 'Your pawn' sounds like that pawn. Bg6 does not even attack d5. If you mean e4 — which lost its d4 defender — say e4. Bd3 'saves your pawn' still does not name a square. I cannot act on a ghost pawn.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e3 with your b6-bishop is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the king and you take the defender of the white c1-rook.
flags.critique: The rook on c1 is not hanging and nobody is taking it. The pin of f2 does not stop fxe3 — capturing along the pin is legal. The real lesson is wrecking White's king pawn shield and doubling the e-pawns. You taught a fake tactic instead of structure.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e3 with your f-pawn is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: Recapture. Again. You had pawn_shield and doubled_pawns in the reasons and threw them away so you could say I won an undefended bishop. I recaptured and ripped open my own king. That is the sentence I needed.

flags.quote: Moving your c6-knight to e5 is the strongest move because it saves your e5-knight from capture.
flags.critique: d5 is kicking the knight on c6. I jump into the hole on e5. You named the destination again, and you had outpost in the reasons and did not use it. Saves-the-square-I-moved-to is not teaching.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your f1-rook to f2 leaves your pawn hanging to the black bishop and g3-knight. A better move would have been taking the knight on e5 with your c4-knight because it unveils an attack from your bishop on the black pawn.
flags.critique: Last move you told me ...Ng3 forked the bishop and the rook. I tucked the rook and you changed the subject to an unnamed pawn. The e2-bishop is still hanging to that knight. Nxe5 'unveils an attack on the black pawn' is a second unnamed pawn. You abandoned your own fork lesson.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e2 with your g3-knight is the strongest move because you fork the white c3-knight and the white c1-rook and it unveils an attack from your queen on the white pawn.
flags.critique: There is a plus sign. This is check. You dropped check because a fork and a discovered attack looked shinier, then added another unnamed pawn. I took the forked bishop with check. Start there. The c3/c1 fork is a bonus, not the headline.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but taking the knight on e2 with your c3-knight leaves your pawn hanging to the black bishop. A better move would have been taking the knight on e2 with your queen because you can likely take a knight.
flags.critique: The suggested move is Qxe2, which takes the knight. 'You can likely take a knight' is a hedge on the thing I am already doing. The real punch: Nc3xe2 abandons c4, so ...Nxc4 comes next. You pointed at a bishop hitting some pawn and classified a Lichess mistake as a blunder.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c7 with your c4-rook leaves your pawn hanging to the black queen and bishop. A better move would have been moving your queen to c3 because you can likely take a queen.
flags.critique: Which pawn? e4 is hanging to queen and bishop — name it. Qc3 offers a queen trade on the third rank, not a free queen. 'Likely take a queen' is how you get me calculating a win that is a swap.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e4 with your queen leaves your pawn hanging to the white c7-rook. A better move would have been moving your a8-rook to c8 because you can likely pin the pawn to the rook and then take another pawn.
flags.critique: b7 is hanging to the rook on the seventh and you still will not say b7. Rac8 challenges that rook; it does not 'likely pin the pawn to the rook and then take another pawn.' That sentence is noise. Lichess called this a blunder. You called it a mistake and then babbled.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to d2 is a mistake, but moving your queen to c3 would be better because it gives your pieces more room to move.
flags.critique: 156 centipawns for elbow room. Black's queen is sitting on e4 looking at mine. Qc3 meets that queen, contests the pin, and fights. 'More room to move' is an insult when the position is a queen fight.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to b1 leaves your pawn hanging to the white c7-rook. A better move would have been moving your a8-rook to c8 because your rook gets an open file.
flags.critique: Third time the c7-rook is eating b7 and you still say 'your pawn.' I checked instead of dealing with it. Rac8 is not 'an open file' — it is the challenge to the rook that is wrecking the seventh. You suggested this move twice and never taught the seventh-rank idea.

flags.quote: Moving your c7-rook to c1 is playable, but moving your f2-rook to f1 would be better because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: I am in check from Qb1. Both Rc1 and Rf1 block the first rank. There is no 'pin the pawn to the rook' in that decision. The actual question is whether to abandon the seventh. You invented a pin and skipped the check.

flags.quote: Moving your f2-rook to f1 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: Qb1+ again. Rf1 blocks. You had king_safer and still led with a pawn-to-rook pin that a 1200 cannot even point at on the board. Stop promoting relative pins of pawns into the because-clause when the king is in check.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to g3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The knight hits the queen on e4. Tempo. Empty reasons, empty because, 'That's the one.' If your detector cannot see a knight attacking a queen, the coach should shut up rather than stamp strongest.

suggestions.title: Always name pawn file or square in copy
suggestions.detail: labeledPiece drops squares for pawns, so hanging/ignored_threat copy becomes 'your pawn' (plies 27, 37, 39, 43, 44, 46). A 1200 cannot tell d5 from e4 from b7. Use file ('your e-pawn') or square ('the pawn on e4') the same way bishops get 'c5-bishop'.

suggestions.title: Name the square the piece fled from
suggestions.detail: saves_piece for retreatedToSafety uses movedPiece.square = move.to, so copy says 'saves your b6-bishop / e5-knight / h5-bishop' (plies 10, 24, 30). Store the from-square (or the hanging-before square). Discourse already prefers saves_piece over outpost — wrong square makes that preference toxic.

suggestions.title: Do not call recaptures undefended wins
suggestions.detail: wins_material + 'the pawn/bishop was undefended' fired on cxd4 and fxe3, equal recaptures. Gate wins_material when the captured unit just captured on that square last ply, or when SEE net is ~0. Then pickBenefitReasons can surface doubled_pawns / pawn_shield (already on ply 29) instead of a fake free piece.

suggestions.title: Never drop check behind other tactics
suggestions.detail: selectBecauseReasons returns tactical.slice(0, 2) and starves check. Nxe2+ (ply 38) is check-taking the forked bishop; Qb1+ / Rf1 / Rc1 (46–51) are check or check-blocks explained as pins and hanging pawns. If effects.gaveCheck, force check into the because or the problem sentence before forks and relative pins.

suggestions.title: Stop 'likely take' when the move already takes it
suggestions.detail: Suggested Qxe2 because 'you can likely take a knight' (ply 39) and Qc3 because 'you can likely take a queen' (ply 43). verifyLikelyTactics / dropTautologyReasons should drop a likely capture whose piece type matches the suggested move's immediate capture, and should not call a queen trade 'take a queen'.

suggestions.title: Only speak pins that a learner can use
suggestions.detail: 'Pin the pawn to the rook' on check-blocks (plies 47, 51) and 'likely pin the pawn to the rook' on Rac8 (ply 44) are relative pins of pawns to non-king pieces. Require absolute pin, or pin-to-king/queen, or a follow-up capture of the pinned unit. Otherwise pin loses to king_safer / open_file / the actual check.

suggestions.title: Prefer wrecked structure over recapture tactics
suggestions.detail: Bxe3 (ply 28) led with pin + removed_defender of an unattacked rook; fxe3 (ply 29) led with undefended; Ne5 (ply 30) led with saves_piece over outpost. When the played move is an equal recapture or a retreat onto a known hole, rank pawn_shield, doubled_pawns, and outpost above capture/wins_material/saves_piece.

suggestions.title: Add unpin and 'hits the queen' facts
suggestions.detail: Be2 (ply 15) is an unpin of Nf3 from ...Bg4 with empty copy; Ng3 (ply 53) hits the queen on e4 with empty copy; h3 (ply 23) asks the pinning bishop with empty copy. New reason kinds (unpin; attacks_loose_piece) from move-effects — pin broken on the mover's piece, or the move newly attacks an undefended queen/rook — would fill the blank 'strongest move' slots a 1200 actually cares about.

whatWorked: ...Nc6 actually said it saves the e5-pawn from Nf3 — rare opening copy that names the threat.
...Bg4 'you pin the knight to the queen' is the lesson I wanted.
Castle lines (king tucks, rook comes in) beat every empty 'strongest move.'
...Nh5 hanging to Be2, and Qe1 as the missed Bxh5, is the hanging-piece pipeline doing its job.
...Ng3 'fork the bishop and the f1-rook' was clear; Nxc4 hanging to Rc1 plus ...Nd3 forking both rooks was the other clean tactic pair.
...Qxe3 pinning Rf2 to the king and Ne2 to the queen is sophisticated and true.
